claim: On September 6, 2001, put-option volume for UAL, the parent company of United Airlines, exceeded call-option volume by more than 20 to 1. The 9/11 Commission reported that one U.S. investment adviser placed 95 percent of that day's UAL put volume as part of a broader airline-trading strategy. The Securities and Exchange Commission and FBI investigated the UAL and American Airlines trades and reported no evidence of illicit trading or advance knowledge of the attacks.

sources.label: National Commission on Terrorist Attacks Upon the United States (9/11 Commission) — Staff Monograph, “The Financing of the 9/11 Plot” (Appendix A)
sources.quote: the UAL put option volume was much higher than any surrounding day and exceeded the call option volume by more than 20 times
